Obesity is a multi-system disorder defined by an elevated body mass index:

Normal BMI: 18-25

Overweight: 25-30

Obese: 30-40

Morbid Obesity \>40

Increased body mass 20%LBM 80%adipose 

Overall ↑respiratory demand  with ↓ Respiratory reserve

Morbid Obesity causes several effects to the respiratory system:

Airway:

- Increased neck and soft tissue leads to ↑ risk of OSA 
- Increased risk of reflux and aspiration 
- Increased risk of difficult BMV and intubation 

Lung Volumes and Capacities 

- ↓FRC \~ 25% \@BMI 30and ↓ERV - worse supine or with GA
- Decreased chest wall compliance due to increased mass/weight of chest wall 
- Decreased lung compliance secondary to basal atelectasis 
- If FRC \<CC → ↑ shunt 
- Rapid desaturation and after induction

Ventilation

- ↑airway resistance due to decreased airway radius at lower lung volumes 
- ↓FRC - Closing capacity differential as FRC is reduced, gas trapping may start to occur causing ↑ A-A gradient. 
- ↑MV requirements due to ↑VO2 and VCO2 from increased body mass 
- Increased work of breathing due to ↓compliance and ↑resistance
- Obesity related hypoventilation - inc PaCO2 levels due to blunting of respiratory reflexes ↓respiratory five 

Pulmonary Circulation 

- Increased risk of pulmonary hypertension secondary to hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction
